preamble: The diphthong [oi] becomes [ei] when its rounded back nucleus unrounds and fronts toward the following [i] offglide. In Old Latin, *oi (and *ai) in unstressed syllables had merged into ei by historical times; this ei later became ī. The o-stem nominative plural therefore appears as -ei (campei < campoi; virei, foideratei in the Senatus consultum de Bacchanalibus, 186 BC), Classical -ī, and the dative/ablative plural -ois became -eis, Classical -īs; the older -oi survives only in the late spelling poploe 'peoples'.

examples.from: o-stem nominative plural *campoi 'fields' (< PIE pronominal *-oi; cf. relic poploe 'peoples')
examples.to: campei; inscriptional virei 'men', foideratei 'allied' (Senatus consultum de Bacchanalibus) > Classical virī, foederātī
examples.note: In unstressed syllables *oi merged with ei, which then raised via ẹ̄ to ī.
The a-stem ending *-ais > -eis > -īs was remodelled on this o-stem ending.
